title:
Comment of Keri Harris in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152229.txt
documents.text:
Keri Harris, Skagway, AK.
My family and I are strongly opposed to this project.

This project will take up 2.5 square miles in the narrowest section of the Cook Inlet. The waste heat from this data center would be absorbed by the Cook Inlet, which would have a negative impact on the marine life sensitive to warm waters. 

This could have serious economic impacts on our communities. The Alaska Department of Fish and Game estimates the total value of Upper Cook Inlet commercial salmon fisheries to average $25 million annually over the last three years. These fisheries will almost certainly be impacted, and those effects will increase over time as generations of salmon are impacted. 

Endangered beluga whales also pass through the bottleneck seasonally to access feeding and calving grounds. The DeepGreen data center would become a significant source of noise, disorienting marine mammals who depend on quiet waterways to communicate, navigate, hunt, and escape predators.

Keep Alaska wild!
